2609.31349.title: DyMD: Preserving Interaction Dynamics through Distribution Matching Distillation in Few-Step Video World Models
2609.31349.paper_summary: Large video diffusion models offer expressive priors for embodied prediction and learning, yet their many-step sampling remains costly for interactive downstream use. Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) enables few-step video generation, but can suppress robot--object motion while preserving visual quality. Examining DMD's teacher and fake-score signals, we find that weak re-noising keeps the teacher posterior concentrated near motion-deficient rollouts, limiting motion-restoring guidance. Meanwhile, stronger-motion rollouts tend to incur larger fake-score fitting errors, which can hinder the generator's learning of interaction dynamics. We propose DyMD, a DMD framework that adapts both teacher supervision and critic fitting to the evolving student. Temporal affinity--conditioned re-noise sampling adapts the timestep distribution to each rollout's current interaction fidelity by mixing the base schedule with a teacher prior motivated by local posterior variation, thereby balancing motion recovery and appearance refinement. To better track stronger-motion rollouts, dynamics-guided fake-score tracking uses a noise-conditioned predictor to estimate noise-relative fitting difficulty from latent temporal dynamics, then upweights predicted-hard rollouts in the critic loss. Using DyMD, we distill a 14B teacher into a four-step 1.3B student with no auxiliary modules at inference. On embodied-video benchmarks, the student improves R-Bench task adherence by $9.6$ percentage points and PAI-Bench-G Domain score by $5.1$ points over Base DMD while maintaining comparable visual quality. As a backbone for downstream action planning, our student achieves 34% mean success across two WorldArena tasks, compared with 16% for Base DMD.
2609.31349.paper_summary_zh: 大型視頻擴散模型為具身預測和學習提供了表達豐富的先驗，但其多步取樣在互動下游使用中仍然代價高昂。分佈匹配蒸餾（DMD）使得少步視頻生成成為可能，但在保持視覺質量的同時可能會抑制機器人與物體的運動。檢查DMD的教師和假分數信號，我們發現弱再噪聲使教師後驗集中在運動不足的展開附近，限制了運動恢復的指導。同時，強運動的展開往往會產生較大的假分數擬合誤差，這可能會妨礙生成器對互動動態的學習。我們提出了DyMD，一種DMD框架，根據不斷發展的學生調整教師監督和評論擬合。時間親和性條件下的再噪聲取樣通過將基礎計劃與受當地後驗變化驅動的教師先驗混合，將時間步分佈調整到每個展開的當前互動保真度，從而平衡運動恢復和外觀精煉。為了更好地跟蹤強運動的展開，動態引導的假分數跟蹤使用噪聲條件預測器來估計來自潛在時間動態的噪聲相關擬合難度，然後在評論損失中加權預測困難的展開。使用DyMD，我們將一個140億的教師蒸餾成一個四步的13億學生，推理時沒有輔助模塊。在具身視頻基準上，學生在R-Bench任務遵循度上提高了9.6個百分點，在PAI-Bench-G領域得分上提高了5.1分，同時保持了可比的視覺質量。作為下游行動規劃的骨幹，我們的學生在兩個WorldArena任務中實現了34%的平均成功率，而Base DMD則為16%。
